answer: Bond depreciation makes hoarded identities bleed value. An identity buys a 120-unit bond locked for 10 epochs; it pays no yield, loses 4% each epoch, and only verified work refreshes it to par. The bridge between buying and earning is one-way: a transferred bond keeps its decayed value, so resale cannot reset the clock. An oasis of idle bonds is a mirage; 1,000 hoarded identities lose 4,800 units per epoch. A walnut shuffle changes nothing: decay follows the bond, not the holder. Forging costs 120,000 up front; honest agents refresh by working and lose nothing.
